paras: The killing of Abe Barner was the fatal shooting of the Rev. Abe Barner, a Black evangelist, and the wounding of his companion Percy Goodlow on a country road near Eufaula, McIntosh County, Oklahoma, on the morning of August 22, 1920. The shots were fired from ambush with a repeating shotgun, and a man named Millard Stafford was arrested and charged with the shooting the same day. The case is known from a brief Muskogee dispatch printed in two Oklahoma dailies.

According to the Muskogee dispatch dated August 23, Barner was "shot to death on a country road near Eufaula" on the previous morning. Goodlow, described as "a companion," was shot five times and seriously wounded. The gunfire came from a repeating shotgun, and whoever fired it escaped into the woods. Neither printing gives a motive or says whether the victims knew their attacker.

Sheriff E. W. McCune arrested Millard Stafford "a short time later" and charged him with the shooting. The reports do not give Stafford's race, and no report of an inquest, hearing, or trial appears in the coverage.

Both known printings appeared on August 23, 1920, and carried the same wire text with small differences. The Daily Ardmoreite ran it as a page-three brief headed "Negro Preacher Shot from Ambush," while the Guthrie Daily Leader placed it on its front page as "Negro Evangelist Is Assassinated." Both identified Barner as "a negro evangelist" and added no comment of their own. No account of the shooting was found in the Black press.

The two printings disagree on several details: the Ardmoreite names the victim Abe Barner, aged 60, and his companion Percy Goodlow, while the Guthrie paper prints "Abe Barnes, 40" and "Perry Goodlow." The Ardmoreite also refers to a single "assailant," whereas the Guthrie text speaks of "assailants," though both report only one arrest. Because both versions descend from one dispatch, the texts alone do not show which details are correct.

accounts.label: Muskogee wire report
accounts.gist: A Black evangelist was shot dead and his companion wounded from ambush on a country road near Eufaula by a gunman (or gunmen) with a repeating shotgun who fled into the woods; Millard Stafford was arrested and charged.

framing.detail: The Ardmoreite ran it as a short page-3 brief headed 'NEGRO PREACHER SHOT FROM AMBUSH'; the Guthrie Daily Leader put it on page 1 as 'Negro Evangelist Is Assassinated'; neither added comment or a motive.
